title: Convert Sorted List to BST
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list whose elements are sorted in **strictly increasing** order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree (BST) and return its root.

To guarantee a unique output tree, for every contiguous sublist of `m` nodes (0-indexed `0 .. m - 1`), select the node at index `floor(m / 2)` as the root of that subtree (for even `m`, this is the right-middle node reached by standard slow/fast pointers both initialized at the sublist head).
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 2000].
Values in the linked list are strictly increasing.
hints: Using slow/fast pointers to split each sublist at index `floor(m / 2)` builds the exact tree in O(n log n) time.
To reach O(n) time, count the total length `n` first, then simulate an in-order traversal over index range `[lo, hi]` with `mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2`, advancing a single list cursor once per node.

examples.explanation: Middle of [-10, -3, 0, 5, 9] is 0; left [-10, -3] picks right-middle -3 and right [5, 9] picks right-middle 9.
An empty list converts to an empty tree (null).
For [1, 2, 3, 4], index 4//2 = 2 (value 3) is root, left [1, 2] has root 2 with left child 1, and right [4] is 4.
